findings.title: max_budget_usd accepts .nan and .inf
findings.detail: check_declared_keys refuses a budget only when `not _is_num(v) or v <= 0`. YAML `.nan` and `.inf` load as floats: `nan <= 0` is False and `inf <= 0` is False, so both pass validation. declared_settings then copies the value into the request, and build_request's `float(settings.get('max_budget_usd') or 1.0)` keeps nan or inf because both are truthy. A project repo can therefore declare a persona with no budget cap at all, or with a NaN budget handed to the claude CLI. The profile validator has the same gap (profiles.py:146). The new helper copies it onto a new, repo-controlled surface. Today the impact is limited because the queue cannot run declared personas (inert), but A3 will consume these values.

findings.title: build_request scans the declared registry twice; persona and review flag can disagree
findings.detail: For a declared persona, get_persona(...) and is_reviewer(...) each call persona_defs.load_registry, so every definition file and template is re-read and re-validated twice per request. If a definition changes between the two scans (an edit or pull in the main checkout while a request is built), `p` can be a valid reviewer while is_reviewer returns False. The reviewer would then run with the reviewer schema but without the diff, test_files and changed_files context. Using `p.role == 'reviewer'` (or `persona in REVIEWER_PERSONAS or (p.declared is not None and p.role == 'reviewer')`) on the already-resolved Persona removes both the duplicate I/O and the race.
findings.trigger: The main checkout's `.nw/personas/sec_reviewer.yaml` is rewritten with a bad key between get_persona and is_reviewer inside one build_request call.

findings.title: template_sha256 is of the validated bytes, not of the template the prompt renders
findings.detail: _check_template hashes and placeholder-checks the bytes it reads during the scan. Persona.template re-reads the file from disk when the prompt is built. The recorded sha256 (and the role-placeholder confinement) can therefore describe different content than what the agent actually received, which weakens the sha as provenance once A3 records it. The spec defines the sha this way, so this is hardening only.

findings.title: template_sha256 describes the bytes read at scan time, but the prompt is rendered from a later re-read of the file
findings.detail: `persona_defs._check_template` hashes the template bytes while validating. `Persona.template` re-reads `template_file` from disk every time `build_prompt` runs. If the file changes between the registry scan and rendering, `Persona.declared["template_sha256"]` (and the placeholder check) no longer describe the prompt that was sent. Today the hash is only displayed, but it is offered as the identity of the template, and Pipeline A3 may record or trust it. The placeholder confinement from SPEC-0371 has the same TOCTOU, so this is not new risk, but the new field claims more than it can guarantee.

findings.title: A declared model id with a trailing newline passes validation
findings.detail: `check_declared_keys` accepts a model if `MODEL_RE.match(model)` succeeds. `MODEL_RE` ends in `$`, which also matches just before a final `\n`, so a quoted YAML value such as `model: "claude-opus-4-1\n"` validates. It then reaches `RunRequest.model` and the claude argv unchanged and fails at run time instead of at `nw personas validate`. The regex already exists in profiles.py; a definition file is only a new place for such a value to come from. `fullmatch` (or `\Z`) would close it.
